country.evidence_quote: Welcome to ALDA, The history of Ala-ud-Din Academy Girls High School (ALDA) can be traced from 1901, when a small informal school was set up by the women of Mian family for imparting education to the girls of Baghbanpura, Lahore. Now, over a century later, the school is one of the oldest and largest private institutions in the area of Baghbanpura, Lahore, Pakistan. It fulfills the educational needs of students from kindergarten to the secondary level.

external_collaboration.evidence_quote: The Green Junior Club Project Certificate Ceremony at, organized in collaboration with Pakistan Red Crescent Society, celebrated the active participation and dedication of students in promoting environmental awareness and community responsibility. Certificates were awarded to students for their enthusiasm, teamwork, and commitment to creating a greener and more sustainable future through meaningful projects and activities.

ALDA students participated in Lahore Science Mela, organized by Khwarizmi Science Academy, at Crescent Model School Shadman Lahore. Over 200 institutions took part in the event, showcasing innovative ideas, scientific models and creative projects. The mela provided students with an interactive and enriching learning experience, encouraging exploration, creativity and engagement with science and innovation.
